summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-R4 admits no external crate. academic-repository-classification links academic-domain, academic-policy, academic-repository-analysis, academic-repository-correlation and thiserror as product edges, and academic-model-run, academic-repository, academic-untrusted-content and trybuild as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: the four workspace product edges are path packages this repository already builds, and thiserror was admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond thiserror's, and no code generator.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-repository-classification is the P2-R4 boundary: section 18's three classifications and the proof each one may not be published without -- section 18.2's five-step chain as five linked types, section 18.3's trigger, current trigger state, benefit and trade-offs, section 18.4's ProjectConceptRequirement with its satisfied/retired/replaced lifecycle and its ClassificationConflict, and section 17.4's locator migration that preserves the original evidence. It is a separate package from academic-repository-correlation because that crate owns what two lanes of evidence say about each other and this one owns what the user is asked to learn from it; the direction of the edge is what keeps a correlation constructible without a classification and a classification impossible without a correlation.

no_second_ladder_note: Section 17.3's evidence ladder was implemented by P2-R2 and section 17.5's seven relations by P2-R3, and this task adds neither a second ladder nor a second relation vocabulary. Section 18.1's OBSERVED is read out of a P2-R3 RelationEdge whose evidence is a P2-R2 finding at EvidenceTier::Observed and from nothing else, so there is no route from repository bytes to a classification that skips either crate; ObservedProof::of_edge is the one producer and its call sites are pinned at two. Section 18.2's first step is a P2-R2 Finding or an approved P2-R3 IntentDocument, so a requirement inherits P2-R2's refusal of a repository-wide scope rather than restating it.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: EntityKind, MasteryLevel, FreshnessBand and EpistemicStatus. Section 7.4's ontology tiers are what make section 18.2's `단지 backend라는 이유로 Distributed Systems 전체를 요구하지 않는다` structural: RequiredConcept::realizing refuses FIELD and ALIAS, and the fields are private, so no RequiredConcept anywhere in a program is at either tier. The three knowledge-state vocabularies are what the fifth step reads, and UserEvidenceGap has no SUFFICIENT variant to return for a state that is applied, fresh and user-confirmed.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-policy: ContentDigest, for the requirement identity. A materialized ProjectConceptRequirement's identity is a domain-separated digest of the snapshot, the goal, its version and the concept rather than those four joined: RequirementId admits 64 bytes and a snapshot identifier is most of that, so a joined and truncated identity made two requirements differing only in goal version one identity. That collapse was measured failing classification_is_snapshot_and_goal_scoped before this edge existed.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-analysis: P2-R2's Finding, FindingScope, Locator, EvidenceTier, LadderRung, ArtifactScope, SubjectId, RepositoryAnalysis, SymbolRecord, SymbolFingerprint, SymbolKind and SourceSpan. The first step of a proof chain is a finding, the sites of a concrete need are its locators, and locator migration follows P2-R2's own span-independent symbol fingerprint into a new snapshot's symbol table.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository-correlation: P2-R3's Correlation, RelationEdge, EdgeEvidence, EvidenceRelation, IntentDocument, ApprovalStatus and DocumentId. Section 18.1's OBSERVED comes from an edge and from nothing else, and section 18.2's approved-goal basis is an IntentDocument at ApprovalStatus::Approved, so a draft or a withdrawn specification founds no requirement.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-model-run: CalibrationRegistry and its dataset types, to build the fresh calibration P2-R2's OBSERVED rungs require before a finding exists to classify.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-repository: P2-R1's capture_local, SnapshotRequest and the identity types a request carries, so every corpus in the acceptance suite is a frozen snapshot that passed the permission and secret gate rather than a fabricated one.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-untrusted-content: SourceIndex, which P2-R1's capture_local returns and P2-R2's AnalysisInput::of checks every unit against.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Section 18's proofs are types, and the seven cases under crates/repository-classification/tests/compile_fail assert that each refusal is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic. The cases live in this package rather than in academic-scenario's suite, where P2-R2's went, because this crate reaches academic-ledger through P2-R3 and scenario_crate_has_no_writer_dependency refuses academic-scenario that crate through a dev edge as much as a product one.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-repository-classification is a workspace path crate, not an external dependency. It owns section 18's three classifications and, for each, the proof it may not be published without: section 18.2's five-step chain, where each step is a constructor argument of the next taken by value, so a chain with a step left out is a program that does not compile rather than a value that validates badly; section 18.3's contract, whose one constructor takes at least one trigger and at least one trade-off, so a `있으면 좋은 기술` list of names never becomes a contract at all; section 18.4's coexistence rules held as shape, with the observation in its own field so OBSERVED and REQUIRED coexist and the forward-looking half in one slot so REQUIRED and WOULD_BENEFIT_FROM cannot; the ProjectConceptRequirement entity whose transitions consume the value and append to a history that only grows; and the ClassificationConflict a user override opens instead of a reclassification, which is CONTRIBUTING.md rule 2 applied to section 18.4's fifth bullet. Its dependency set is minimal and the edges it does not have are the point: no academic-store, so a classification cannot reach the canonical writer; no academic-worker and no academic-egress-boundary, so nothing in its closure can launch a process or stage a payload.
network_posture: The crate opens no socket, opens no file, declares no foreign function, reads no environment variable, spawns no process, and runs no build script. It spells no std::fs name at all: every artifact arrives as an argument, the way P2-R3's documents do. the_classification_crate_touches_no_file_and_no_socket in crates/repository-classification/tests/classification_scans.rs compares the whole set of its use items, the whole set of the two-segment paths it reaches through a crate root, and the whole set of the macros it invokes against pinned inventories in both directions, and runs a whole-identifier pass for filesystem and transport constructs over every file of the package, tests included. Three separate injections that spell none of the forbidden tokens and add no listed name were each observed failing it -- a whitespace-separated absolute filesystem path with no use item, a compile-time include_str! file read, and a filesystem type imported under a harmless alias -- and a fourth, a field holding analyzed bytes under a name no alternation lists, was observed failing every_field_of_this_crate_is_in_the_inventory. Its link closure holds nothing that can open a socket beyond libc, which reaches it through academic-policy's bundled SQLite by way of academic-repository. Every snapshot, corpus, document, goal, override and requirement in its test tree is synthetic and built in process; no real repository is read and no network call is made.
advisory_path: Unchanged. Every external crate academic-repository-classification links was admitted by an earlier receipt and is triaged through that receipt's advisory path. trybuild is a dev dependency already admitted for academic-scenario, academic-desktop and academic-proposal. .github/dependabot.yml opens no version-update pull request.
